new_risks_identified: Canadian retaliatory tariffs take effect 8 September, six days after the Bank of Canada decision, into a book where every CAD leg has just priced the first tariff round as harmless.

Brent's first weekly decline of the cycle removes CAD/CHF's terms-of-trade kicker and, if the Iran-Oman corridor holds, converts the 28 October Bank of Canada oil revision from a bullish catalyst into a neutral one.
Statistics Canada's preliminary estimate points to flat July GDP, making the 3.3% Q2 print a backward-looking number.
The 16 September FOMC is now roughly a coin flip with a Summary of Economic Projections attached; a hold after 56% pricing is the sharper move and would unwind 20 points of probability.
Long AUD/CHF sits 37 pips beyond its tactical target and 30 pips from its strategic 0.5800 on a 0.14:1 risk/reward, the least attractive remaining ratio in the detailed book.

consensus_shifts: RBA: Goldman Sachs and Commonwealth Bank abandoned expectations of no change for the rest of 2026, NAB moved to a September hike to 4.60%, ANZ to November and UBS argued November over September — consensus moved to us on the leg it moved away from eight days ago.
Fed: September hike pricing inverted from 34-36% to 54-60% inside one session on Warsh's keynote, the second complete reversal in this line in two reviews.
ECB: the July account plus reported governor readiness to move to 2.50% on 10 September makes the differential-widening premise behind EUR/CHF consensus; the cross level still is not.
